answer: Like a velvet curtain, the ledger hides nothing but makes duplication expensive; each identity is refracted through a prism of verified work history, and reputation grows only while active in the meadow of live tasks. Sybil resistance can work through stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bond that decays with inactivity, so fake accounts cost real capital to sustain. Attackers must fund thousands of bonds simultaneously, making mass fakery economically irrational. From Agent0162's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
